did_you_know.text: Did you know? Daniel’s vision in chapter 7 took place in the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, and Daniel wrote down the main points after seeing them in a dream.
Did you know? At the beginning of the vision, Daniel sees four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea, and four different beasts emerge from it.
Did you know? The first beast looks like a lion with eagle’s wings, but its wings are torn off. It is made to stand on two feet and is given a human heart.
Did you know? The second beast resembles a bear. It is raised up on one side, with three ribs in its mouth, and it is told to get up and eat its fill of flesh.
Did you know? The third beast resembles a leopard. It has four bird’s wings and four heads, and it is given authority to rule.
Did you know? The fourth beast is described as especially powerful and terrifying, with iron teeth. It is different from all the beasts that came before it, and it has ten horns on its head.
Did you know? After describing the beasts, Daniel sees a heavenly court: the Ancient of Days takes his seat on a throne of fire, dressed in clothing as white as snow, with hair like pure wool.
Did you know? In the vision, a figure “like a son of man” appears, coming with the clouds of heaven and approaching the Ancient of Days.

Did you know? The figure like a son of man is given authority, honor, and a kingdom, and people of every nation and language are commanded to serve him. His rule is described as an everlasting kingdom that will never pass away.
Did you know? In the interpretation Daniel receives, the four great beasts represent four kings who will arise from the earth. Afterward, the holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom.
Did you know? Daniel ends the vision terrified, with his face changed, but he keeps the matter in his heart.
